data.narrative:
Renaissance Fusion is a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Francesco Volpe and Martin Kupp, having raised $60.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 private and 3 public nuclear energy firms, including peers such as Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo (OKLO).

Given the early-stage nature of Renaissance Fusion and the heterogeneity of nuclear technology approaches across the sector, peer-median valuation proved inapplicable. The narrow peer set—only one same-stage comparable and one adjacent-stage company—falls short of the minimum three datapoints required for reliable median triangulation. A stage-progression methodology was applied instead, using the company's $60.5M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $121M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $103M to $139M, with $121M as the median point. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression anchor. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of sufficiently comparable Series A peers in the nuclear sector, which limits the ability to benchmark against direct developmental stage and capital intensity analogues. Technology risk, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital requirements for demonstration phases remain material but unquantified in this analysis.
